title: Home
description: NOC home / wall-TV command board — Live System Status. Top row: the US datacenter map, full width. Bottom band (left→right): per-zone SIP VIP reachability + servers up/down (East · West · Central), carrier trunks (Bandwidth Dallas / LA, Sinch Denver / Chicago origination), platform services. 🟢 green = healthy · 🔴 red = attention · 🟠 orange = stale probe. Zone tiles: VIP reachable (uptime pass-fraction ≥ 99.9%) + one UP/DOWN box per server (SBC-1 · SBC-2 · FS-1 · FS-2 · SVCS/DB) pinned to the expected fleet — a server that stops reporting goes RED, it never vanishes. Carrier tiles: UP / DOWN from live Kamailio-dispatcher OPTIONS probes + inbound calls landed in the last hour. Platform services: UP / DOWN from live blackbox probes. Map: 🟢 datacenter (dot size = calls / hour) · 🔺 carrier trunk (Bandwidth 🟢 up · Sinch 🔵 up · 🔴 down) — includes the two Sinch termination trunks (Atlanta LD, Denver TF; the two Denver triangles are offset — orig west / label above, TF east / label below). Below the band, three full-width KPI rows: Traffic (active calls · CPS · calls 1h/today · ASR · on-net %), Voice (MOS · loss · peak jitter · R-factor · ACD · PDD-proxy p95), and STIR/SHAKEN (signed % · A share · div chains · inbound verified % · trust-bundle age · leaf-cert time left). Hover any tile or map marker for detail. Landing page for the Production NOC.

panels.title: Platform services
panels.description: Live blackbox-probe status of the platform's core services (probe_success from VictoriaMetrics). Each cell is one probed service — 🟢 UP (probe_success=1) · 🔴 DOWN (0 or no data). Renders every service label automatically (API · ClickHouse · Homer qryn · Homer HEP · Grafana · VictoriaMetrics · any added later).

panels.title: East · us-east1
panels.description: East datacenter status. Headline: SIP VIP 34.24.133.82:5060 carrier reachability (GCM uptime check pass-fraction; Reachable >= 99.9%). Below: one box per server — SBC-1/SBC-2 (Kamailio, east-sbc-1/east-sbc-2), FS-1 (fs-media-v2) / FS-2 (east-fs-2 media-HA hot standby), SVCS (services VM: PG primary + API + UI + Homer, reporting_instance east-services), DB (east-db-standby). Per-server source: VictoriaMetrics up{job="node"} per reporting_instance, freshness-clamped with last_over_time(...[2m]) and pinned to the expected fleet via `or vector(0)` per server — a VM whose metrics go silent (VM dead, node_exporter dead, or vmagent dark/wedged-buffering > 2m) renders a RED DOWN box, it never vanishes. (Plain `up` would return a stale value for VictoriaMetrics' 5m lookback and then disappear entirely; the [2m] clamp turns 'silent 2m' into absent and the synthetic vector(0) arm turns absent into 0=DOWN — the two compose rather than fight.) Canonical job is node_exporter (present on every VM) so each server yields exactly one box; max() guards against dupes. Boxes are VM/metrics-plane liveness, NOT SIP election — the active/standby SBC + FS election rows live on Traffic & Status. EXCEPTION — the DB box: east-db-standby runs NO metrics plane (docker-compose.db.yml covers west-db/central-db only; no vmagent/node_exporter there), so instead of faking an `up` series its box is driven live from the East PRIMARY via voip-cdr-pg: slot east_standby active AND streaming in pg_stat_replication — an honest, arguably stronger signal (catches Postgres down even while the VM is up, and detection is instant, no staleness window). If the primary itself is unreachable the whole query errors loudly rather than showing a stale green. East holds the DB primary + API + UI.

targets.rawSql: SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE s.active AND r.state = 'streaming') AS standby_up FROM pg_replication_slots s LEFT JOIN pg_stat_replication r ON r.pid = s.active_pid WHERE s.slot_name = 'east_standby';

panels.title: BW Dallas
panels.description: Bandwidth Dallas trunk (67.231.2.12, primary). Top: live reachability from the SBCs' Kamailio-dispatcher OPTIONS probes (carrier_trunk_health, duid bw-dallas-primary) — 🟢 UP (reachable from ≥1 SBC) · 🔴 DOWN (dead on every SBC) · 🟠 STALE (no fresh probe in 90s). Proactive, independent of call traffic. Bottom: inbound calls landed via this PoP in the last hour (cdrs, inbound_carrier='bandwidth', pop='dallas').

targets.rawSql: SELECT CASE WHEN status IS NULL THEN 2 WHEN last_updated IS NULL OR last_updated < now() - interval '90 seconds' THEN 2 WHEN status = 'up' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS carrier_up FROM carrier_trunk_health WHERE duid = 'bw-dallas-primary';
SELECT count(*) AS calls_1h FROM cdrs WHERE start_time > now() - interval '1 hour' AND direction = 'inbound' AND inbound_carrier = 'bandwidth' AND inbound_carrier_pop = 'dallas';

panels.title: Sinch DEN
panels.description: Sinch Denver ORIGINATION trunk (206.146.100.24, TG DNVTCOZIGR2_3278). Top: passive-OR-probe health (carrier_trunk_health, duid sinch-denver) — 🟢 UP (OPTIONS probe answered from ≥ 1 SBC, OR inbound calls landed via this PoP in the last 60 min — passive evidence) · 🟡 PASSIVE (no probe answer AND no recent traffic — this orig-only TG was provisioned Sinch→us and does not answer OPTIONS from unregistered IPs, so 'down' is unknowable from our side; NOT an outage signal) · 🟠 STALE (no fresh probe report in 90s — monitoring pipeline dark) · 🔴 DOWN is unreachable for this trunk unless Sinch enables OPTIONS response toward our SBC IPs (then strict probe truth returns). Bottom: inbound calls landed via this PoP in the last hour (cdrs, inbound_carrier='sinch', pop='denver') — the Sinch orig test TN 5305480845 lands here.

targets.rawSql: SELECT CASE WHEN status IS NULL THEN 2 WHEN last_updated IS NULL OR last_updated < now() - interval '90 seconds' THEN 2 WHEN status = 'up' THEN 1 WHEN status = 'passive' THEN 3 ELSE 0 END AS carrier_up FROM carrier_trunk_health WHERE duid = 'sinch-denver';
SELECT count(*) AS calls_1h FROM cdrs WHERE start_time > now() - interval '1 hour' AND direction = 'inbound' AND inbound_carrier = 'sinch' AND inbound_carrier_pop = 'denver';

panels.title: US datacenters · live regions, carriers & traffic
panels.description: Geographic view of the 3 GCP datacenters (green, sized by calls in the last hour) and every carrier trunk — Bandwidth (Dallas primary, LA secondary) plus all 4 Sinch PoPs: origination Denver (TG DNVTCOZIGR2_3278) and Chicago (CHCGIL24GR4_7412), termination Atlanta LD (ATLNGAQSGR2_7214) and Denver TF (DNVTCOZIGR2_3282, toll-free 8YY only, priority below Bandwidth). Bandwidth + Sinch TERMINATION triangles are colored by the SBCs' live Kamailio-dispatcher OPTIONS probes (carrier_trunk_health): Bandwidth GREEN when up, Sinch termination BLUE when up; RED when the trunk is down on every SBC or its status is stale (no fresh probe in 90s) / not yet reported. Sinch ORIGINATION triangles (Denver orig + Chicago) use passive-OR-probe health instead (migration 45): BLUE when the probe is answered OR inbound calls landed via that PoP in the last 60 min, YELLOW 'PASSIVE' when neither — these orig-only TGs were provisioned Sinch→us and do not answer OPTIONS from unregistered IPs, so 'down' is unknowable and never rendered red; RED on an orig triangle only means stale/unreported monitoring. Denver hosts BOTH a Sinch origination PoP and the TF termination trunk — the two triangles are offset slightly (orig west / label above, TF east / label below) so both stay legible at TV distance. Probe coloring is proactive and independent of call traffic, so a dead probed carrier shows even at zero volume. Hover a triangle for status, SBCs up / reporting, seconds since last probe, and (origination) inbound calls in the last hour. Datacenter up/down, VIP reachability and servers up/down are the zone tiles in the band below the map; Bandwidth + Sinch origination health/volume are the carrier tiles in that band.

targets.rawSql: SELECT z.name, z.lat, z.lon, COALESCE(c.calls,0) AS calls_1h FROM (VALUES ('East',33.13::float8,-80.01::float8,'east'),('West',45.60::float8,-121.18::float8,'west'),('Central',41.26::float8,-95.86::float8,'central')) AS z(name,lat,lon,zk) LEFT JOIN (SELECT split_part(coalesce(sbc_id,''),'-',1) AS zone, count(*) AS calls FROM cdrs WHERE start_time > now() - interval '1 hour' GROUP BY 1) c ON c.zone=z.zk;

SELECT COALESCE(h.name, z.name) AS name, z.lat, z.lon, CASE WHEN h.status = 'up' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS up, COALESCE(h.status,'unknown') AS status, COALESCE(h.up_sbcs,0) AS up_sbcs, COALESCE(h.total_sbcs,0) AS total_sbcs, CASE WHEN h.last_updated IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE round(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (now() - h.last_updated)))::int END AS probe_age_s FROM (VALUES ('bw-dallas-primary','Bandwidth Dallas',32.78::float8,-96.80::float8),('bw-la-secondary','Bandwidth LA',34.05::float8,-118.24::float8)) AS z(duid,name,lat,lon) LEFT JOIN carrier_trunk_health h ON h.duid = z.duid ORDER BY z.duid;

SELECT COALESCE(h.name, z.name) AS name, z.lat, z.lon, CASE WHEN h.status = 'up' THEN 1 WHEN h.status = 'passive' THEN 2 ELSE 0 END AS sinch_up, COALESCE(h.status,'unknown') AS status, COALESCE(h.up_sbcs,0) AS up_sbcs, COALESCE(h.total_sbcs,0) AS total_sbcs, CASE WHEN h.last_updated IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE round(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (now() - h.last_updated)))::int END AS probe_age_s, COALESCE(h.recent_inbound_calls,0) AS inbound_1h FROM (VALUES ('sinch-denver','Sinch Denver',39.74::float8,-105.70::float8),('sinch-chicago','Sinch Chicago',41.88::float8,-87.63::float8)) AS z(duid,name,lat,lon) LEFT JOIN carrier_trunk_health h ON h.duid = z.duid ORDER BY z.duid;

SELECT COALESCE(h.name, z.name) AS name, z.lat, z.lon, CASE WHEN h.status = 'up' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS sinch_up, COALESCE(h.status,'unknown') AS status, COALESCE(h.up_sbcs,0) AS up_sbcs, COALESCE(h.total_sbcs,0) AS total_sbcs, CASE WHEN h.last_updated IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE round(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (now() - h.last_updated)))::int END AS probe_age_s FROM (VALUES ('sinch-atlanta-ld','Sinch Atlanta LD',33.75::float8,-84.39::float8),('sinch-denver-tf','Sinch Denver TF',39.74::float8,-104.30::float8)) AS z(duid,name,lat,lon) LEFT JOIN carrier_trunk_health h ON h.duid = z.duid ORDER BY z.duid;

panels.title: Traffic · Active calls — now
panels.description: Live connected calls platform-wide: sum(freeswitch_calls_active) across every FS node, all zones — the same live gauge as Traffic & Status id 3 (ESL exporter :9103). Volume metric, informational blue. Sparkline shows the dashboard range.

panels.title: Traffic · CPS — now (1m)
panels.description: Live calls-per-second, all zones: sum(zone:kamailio_trunk_cps:rate1m) — the vmalert recording rule over kamailio_trunk_cps (INVITE admits per carrier trunk), same query as Traffic & Status id 1. Green normal · orange >= 350 · red >= 500 (platform capacity guardrails).

panels.title: Traffic · Calls — last hour
panels.description: CDR count, trailing 60 min, all zones (cdrs.start_time > now()-1h on the East primary — every zone's FS posts CDRs there). Same source as the geomap dot sizing. Informational blue.

targets.rawSql: SELECT count(*) AS calls_1h FROM cdrs WHERE start_time > now() - interval '1 hour';

panels.title: Traffic · Calls — today
panels.description: CDR count since midnight (date_trunc('day', now()) — DB server timezone, not browser). All zones, all directions. Informational blue.

targets.rawSql: SELECT count(*) AS calls_today FROM cdrs WHERE start_time >= date_trunc('day', now());

panels.title: Traffic · ASR — 15m
panels.description: Answer-Seizure Ratio, trailing 15 min, all zones: answered (answer_time set) / all attempts, from CDRs (Call Quality id 40's query with the zone filter dropped — noc-home has no zone variable). CDR-based, so it lags live SIP by CDR ingest; the live SIP-reply ASR is on Traffic & Status. Red < 40% · orange < 55% · green >= 55% (forwarded-call traffic mix runs lower than raw PSTN ASR).

targets.rawSql: SELECT (count(*) FILTER (WHERE answer_time IS NOT NULL))::float / NULLIF(count(*), 0) AS asr FROM cdrs WHERE start_time > now() - interval '15 minutes';

panels.title: Traffic · On-net % — 15m
panels.description: Share of calls delivered on-net (internal short-circuit, no carrier hairpin) in the trailing 15 min, from CDRs.on_net (Call Quality id 44's query, zone filter dropped). Higher = more carrier minutes saved. Informational blue.

targets.rawSql: SELECT (count(*) FILTER (WHERE on_net))::float / NULLIF(count(*), 0) AS on_net_pct FROM cdrs WHERE start_time > now() - interval '15 minutes';

panels.title: Voice · Avg MOS — 15m
panels.description: Mean Opinion Score, trailing 15 min, rated calls only (mos IS NOT NULL), all zones — Call Quality id 43's query with the zone filter dropped. Red < 3.5 · orange < 4.0 · green >= 4.0.

targets.rawSql: SELECT avg(mos) AS avg_mos FROM cdrs WHERE start_time > now() - interval '15 minutes' AND mos IS NOT NULL;

panels.title: Voice · Packet loss — 15m
panels.description: Average RTP packet loss %, trailing 15 min, rated-calls-only semantics per Call Quality conventions (billable_ms >= 10000 AND rtp_audio_in_packet_count >= 500 — short/silent calls produce junk loss numbers). Green < 1% · orange >= 1% · red >= 3%.

targets.rawSql: SELECT avg(packet_loss_pct) AS avg_loss_pct FROM cdrs WHERE start_time > now() - interval '15 minutes' AND packet_loss_pct IS NOT NULL AND billable_ms >= 10000 AND rtp_audio_in_packet_count >= 500;

panels.title: Voice · Peak jitter — 15m
panels.description: Average of per-call PEAK jitter (cdrs.jitter_max_ms — real milliseconds since migration 43's variance->ms fix), trailing 15 min, rated calls only (billable_ms >= 10000, rtp_audio_in_packet_count >= 500), matching Call Quality id 20. Peak latches the worst burst of each call, so this reads pessimistic vs mean jitter. Green < 40 ms · orange >= 40 · red >= 80.

targets.rawSql: SELECT avg(jitter_max_ms) AS avg_peak_jitter_ms FROM cdrs WHERE start_time > now() - interval '15 minutes' AND jitter_max_ms IS NOT NULL AND billable_ms >= 10000 AND rtp_audio_in_packet_count >= 500;

panels.title: Voice · R-factor — 15m
panels.description: Average R-factor (ITU-T G.107 E-model, 0-100), trailing 15 min, rated calls only (r_factor IS NOT NULL) — Call Quality id 13's metric as a stat. Red < 70 (users complain) · orange < 80 · green >= 80 (toll quality).

targets.rawSql: SELECT avg(r_factor) AS avg_r_factor FROM cdrs WHERE start_time > now() - interval '15 minutes' AND r_factor IS NOT NULL;

panels.title: Voice · ACD — 1h
panels.description: Average Call Duration of ANSWERED calls in the trailing hour: avg(end_time - answer_time) from CDRs (true talk time, not billable_ms which carries minimum/increment rounding). ACD shifts are a traffic-mix / fraud signal, not a health threshold — informational blue.

targets.rawSql: SELECT avg(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (end_time - answer_time))) AS acd_sec FROM cdrs WHERE start_time > now() - interval '1 hour' AND answer_time IS NOT NULL AND end_time IS NOT NULL;

panels.title: Voice · PDD p95 (proxy) — 1h
panels.description: CAVEAT — this is time-to-ANSWER (answer_time - start_time, p95 over the trailing hour, Call Quality id 4's proxy), NOT true Post-Dial Delay: it includes human ring time on the forwarded leg, so it reads as an UPPER BOUND on PDD and normally sits in the tens of seconds. True PDD (INVITE->18x) needs SIP-timestamp instrumentation we don't record in CDRs. Watch the TREND: a sudden jump with flat ASR usually means slow carrier PDD (progress_timeout pressure), not slower humans. Informational blue — no red/green judgment on a proxy.

targets.rawSql: SELECT percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (answer_time - start_time))) AS p95_answer_s FROM cdrs WHERE start_time > now() - interval '1 hour' AND answer_time IS NOT NULL;

panels.title: STIR · Signed % — 1h
panels.description: Share of outbound carrier B-legs that left with a SHAKEN Identity header (attestation != unsigned) in the trailing hour: kamailio_stir_attest_signed (counter, NO _total suffix — counts legs actually emitted on the wire; the unsigned bucket is the fail-open path). Red < 80% · orange < 95% · green >= 95% (mirrors the stir-shaken board's 5%/20% unsigned alarm bands, inverted).

panels.title: STIR · Attestation A share — 1h
panels.description: Share of signed+unsigned outbound legs carrying full attestation A (Trunk/API-originated, we know the customer AND the number) in the trailing hour, from kamailio_stir_attest_signed{attestation="A"}. RCF forwards sign as div-chained instead, so A share tracks the Trunk/API traffic mix — informational blue, not a health threshold.

panels.title: STIR · div chains — 1h
panels.description: Count of RCF forwarded legs signed with a div (diversion) PASSporT chained onto the inbound Identity in the trailing hour — the best possible outcome for a forwarded call (preserves the originator's attestation; confirmed end-to-end vs T-Mobile A->div). kamailio_stir_attest_signed{attestation="div"}. Volume tracks RCF forward traffic of signed inbound — informational blue.

panels.title: STIR · Inbound verified % — 1h
panels.description: Share of inbound calls arriving with verstat TN-Validation-Passed in the trailing hour: kamailio_stir_inbound_verstat (counter, NO _total suffix; verstat currently sourced from Bandwidth's P-Attestation-Indicator / PAI verstat until own-crypto trust-bundle verify ships — the stir-shaken board splits self vs carrier). Thresholds copied from stir-shaken id 6: red < 20% · orange < 50% · green >= 50%.

panels.title: STIR · Trust bundle age
panels.description: Age of the last VERIFIED STI-PA trust-bundle install: time() - stir_trust_bundle_installed_timestamp_seconds (textfile metric from refresh-stir-trust-bundle / stir-trust-lib.sh, exported by the services-VM node_exporter --collector.textfile.directory=/var/lib/stir/metrics — the only textfile emitter today; max() keeps this a single box if another exporter ever appears). Same 40d-watchdog bands as stir-shaken id 201: green < 30d · orange >= 30d · red >= 40d (bundle refresh pipeline stuck).

panels.title: STIR · Leaf cert — time left
panels.description: Time until our SHAKEN signing leaf (CN=SHAKEN 8052, Neustar/TruContact-issued) expires: min(stir_leaf_cert_expiry_timestamp_seconds) - time() (same textfile source as the bundle-age tile; min() = worst reporter). Expires 2027-05-08, renewal due ~2027-04-01. Thresholds per stir-shaken id 206: red expired/none · orange < 30d · green >= 60d. If this goes orange, start the Neustar renewal NOW — an expired leaf means every outbound call goes out unsigned.
